newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Aeropostal loses prospective buyer.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Aeropostal loses prospective buyer.

text.p: World Aviation Group, a British air transport company, has withdrawn from participation in the planned sale of Venezuelan airline Aeropostal because it considered the auction process to be too bothersome and unclear, company lawyers said.

"The (airline's) receivers have retarded the process... and World Aviation Group will not be participating although it is prepared to pay $4 million more than the $20 million base price," said Humberto Bauder of Bauder and Associates, a Venezuelan law firm representing the group.
Aeropostal is scheduled to go on the auction block on August 30 after three earlier attempts to sell the airline failed.
"The conditions of the sale have been very strangely managed, which goes against the grain of the receiver's original intention, namely a transparent process," Bauder said.
Bauder, for example, said the policy on returning deposits required to participate in the auction was not clear.

Four other groups have expressed interest in buying the airline: the Venezuelan-U.S. consortium Alas; a group of former Aeropostal pilots and Delta Air Lines executives; Venezuela's Zuliana de Aviacion; and the Venezuelan consortium Cavendes-Laser.
The first attempt to auction the airline failed in July 1994 when the Venezuelan Investment Fund declared void an 80 percent public offering valued at $62 million.
The airline was declared bankrupt and closed in September 1994.
